title: Observability hybrid runbook notes — tracing, dashboards, cost
content:
Context:
A short, portable write-up intended as the hybrid runbook/check-in for the week of 2026-05-28. This merges the on-call handoff, dashboard health check, and cost-telemetry experiments into a single living note so SRE, runtime, and product teams can pick up action items quickly.

Attendees:
- Aisha Patel (notes/lead)
- Miguel Sanchez (tracing lead)
- Rina Kapoor (dashboards)
- Ethan Cho (cost telemetry)
- Samira (on-call cover, SRE)

Agenda:
1) Quick health snapshot (dashboards + alerts)
2) Trace sampling experiment status + immediate adjustments
3) Dashboard debt: widgets to retire/replace this sprint
4) Cost telemetry anomalies and root-cause leads
5) Runbook edits and on-call playbook items

1) Health snapshot (5m)
- Uptime: 99.995% for collector services last 7d.
- Alert noise: 14 untriaged alerts in the observability alert queue (down from 21 last week). Most are high-latency traces from region-us-west2 during the 03:00–04:00UTC DB compaction window.
- Dashboards: Key perf dashboard (tracing-overview) reports 95th token-latency increased by ~8% during compactions; otherwise stable.
- Action: Samira to add a short runbook step to temporarily bump trace-sampling for affected services during scheduled DB compaction (see Actions).

2) Trace sampling experiment (Miguel) (15m)
Summary: We ran a targeted sampling increase on the inference-router and grpc-proxy pods to capture more end-to-end traces for a spike observed 2026-05-20. The change used adaptive sampling: base 0.5% -> burst 5% for error-tagged spans.
Findings to date:
- Increased signal for root-cause analysis; success: found a mis-routed fallback path in the router code that adds ~120ms when model cache misses coincide with cold KV fetches.
- Cost impact: tracer ingestion rate rose +18% for the two-day window, translating to ~+4.5% increase in storage/ingestion cost for traces.
Open questions:
- Should adaptive sampling be permanent for router? (Pros: faster RM; Cons: cost)
- Are there low-cost alternatives (span-level sampling + on-agent enrichment)?

Decision (tentative):
- Keep adaptive burst active for 72h more while fixes are validated in canary. Re-evaluate with cost telemetry at end of period.

3) Dashboard debt and proposed cleanups (Rina) (10m)
- Dashboard inventory audit completed: 62 dashboards, 18 with >75% stale widgets.
- Immediate prunes: retire two dashboards that duplicate per-route latency views (dup-latency-a, dup-latency-b).
- Widget migration: move token-level cost breakdown into a per-model dashboard (new panel) instead of global cost dashboard to reduce cardinality and improve load times.
- UX note: add a small explainer about the token-cost panel to reduce noisy pager escalations.

4) Cost telemetry anomalies (Ethan) (10m)
Recent anomalies: May 21–22 cost spike (~6% week-over-week) driven by a 30% increase in tail retry traffic for a specific customer integration. Root cause tracing shows exponential backoff misconfiguration.
Actions taken:
- Temporary quota bump rolled back for customer.
- Customer CSM contacted; SE assigned to help fix client retry behavior (Linked: JIRA OBS-4198).
Metric snapshot (today):
- Avg ingestion tokens/day: 1.4M
- Ingestion cost trend: +6% W/W (May 21–22), stabilized after quota rollback.

5) Runbook edits (all) (10m)
- New quick-check steps added to runbook (confluence:OBS-Runbook-2026):
  * How to check sampling rates per-service (kubectl + agent api)
  * How to temporarily ramp sampling for a pod via configmap patch (one-liner examples)
  * Pager escalation matrix for trace-collection spikes
- Note to self: include the standard KMS/HSM key path for trace-encryption in the runbook next iteration (security review required).

Decisions and owner assignments:
- Miguel: keep adaptive burst active for +72h (ends 2026-05-31) and produce costing delta (due 2026-06-01) — owner Miguel Sanchez.
- Samira: add a DB-compaction mitigation step to on-call playbook and validate compaction window overlap with collector CPU spikes (due 2026-05-30).
- Rina: retire duplicate dashboards and submit PR with migration plan for token-cost panel (WIP PR: github/pull/678) (due 2026-06-04).
- Ethan: follow up with CSM + open a postmortem ticket for the retry-induced cost spike (JIRA OBS-4198) (initial triage due 2026-05-29).
- Aisha: schedule 30-min follow-up async review and snapshot the cost numbers after the 72h sampling window (meeting: calendar event scheduled 2026-06-02).

Backlog / things to track (short bullets):
- Explore span-level enrichment to reduce ingestion without losing critical error context.
- Prototype deterministic sampling based on model-id and route to reduce noise from high-volume customers.
- Dashboard perf: investigate slow widget query causing UI timeouts for large time ranges (likely due to high-cardinality joins).
- Re-evaluate retention tiers for debug-level traces to reduce long-term storage costs.

Notes-to-self / friction points:
- Need a fast way to diff sampling config across clusters (kubectl + jq script exists but brittle). Consider converting to an internal tiny tool.
- Inter-team comms: Security wants to review any runbook content that mentions KMS/HSM key paths. Don't publish until reviewed.

Quick playbook excerpt (to copy into confluence runbook):
- "If you observe a sudden >15% increase in trace ingestion:
  1) Check sampling overrides: kubectl -n observability get cm tracer-config -o yaml | grep sampling
  2) Query ingest rate by service: SELECT sum(spans) FROM trace_metrics WHERE ts > now() - 1h GROUP BY service (internal query, dashboard quick-link provided)
  3) If root cause is customer retry loop, coordinate with CS to roll back quota bumps and open JIRA for follow-up
  4) If root cause is platform (router fallback), increase sampling to 5% for 24–72h for router only and notify stakeholders

Immediate next sync:
- Asynchronous notes and a quick decisions thread on slack #observability by EOD 2026-05-29. If the cost delta from the sampling window exceeds +9% estimate, we trigger an emergency review.

Attachments / references:
- TEMP: snapshot of the 'token-cost-by-model' panel (export: /tmp/token-cost-2026-05-28.png)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/678
- JIRA: OBS-4198 (customer retry loop)
- Confluence: confluence:OBS-Runbook-2026

End-of-note.

(rough in style: please flag anything that should be escalated to product or runtime — Aisha)
